top_choice_rationale: P002 recognises Kane and Mele for showing that time-reversal-invariant, spin-orbit-coupled insulators carry a Z2 invariant with protected helical edge transport, and Molenkamp for the direct observation of that edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells. It is a prediction followed by an experimental test, with fifteen years of confirmation, and it introduces a new organising principle for phases of matter. The credit is imperfect because Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the three-dimensional work fall outside three names, and the 2016 prize is adjacent, but the citation can separate the Z2 time-reversal-symmetric phase from the 2016 topological-order work. P001 is a close second with a clean two-name credit and independent confirmation, but it is a gain in measurement capability more than a new concept. Any award is preferable to none.
recusal_note: Director of WACQT and professor at Chalmers; colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson and frequent co-author Anton Frisk Kockum are in circuit QED, which is not in this slate. No specific connection to the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp or Katori-Ye credits is apparent from my profile.
